change: trm:tonglen ~ exchange of self and other (partial)
reason: Tonglen is the meditative enactment of the exchange taught in Bodhicaryāvatāra 8.120ff; the Seven Points present it as the relative-bodhicitta practice.
Gorampa's 'free from elaboration' takes up the MMK's pacification of elaborations but extends it to negating all four extremes as a view; the Gelug accepts the MMK phrase but not Gorampa's extension.
The Lamdre view of the causal continuum parallels MMK 25.19–20 but is asserted of the clarity-emptiness of mind realised through tantra.
The same word ālaya/kun gzhi; Sakya reads the Lamdre all-base as clarity-emptiness, the Gelug denies an ālaya-vijñāna in Prāsaṅgika; not equated.
Tibetan nges 'byung renders niḥsaraṇa; in Tsongkhapa it names the attitude of renunciation rather than the escape itself.
Sakya teachers read lines 1–3 of Parting as the three scopes; the correspondence is the Sakya's own.
Renunciation is the middling scope's attitude, bodhicitta the great scope's; Tsongkhapa's letter condenses the lamrim.
The impure-vision topics are those of the small and middling scopes; not an identity of systems.
Gorampa takes his view to be MMK 18.9's pacification of elaborations; the Gelug accepts the phrase but not the unqualified negation.
Tantric (Lamdre) and sūtra (MMK 25.19–20) statements of non-difference; the Sakya holds the tantric realisation to be reached through empowerment and the two stages.
Both turn obstacles into the path; Lamdre does it in completion-stage experience, lojong in daily adversity.
Impure vision banded B0 (turning), experiential B4 (meditative experience), pure B7 (buddha qualities).
Lines 1–4 banded B0/B1/B2/B5 by what each line establishes.
Renunciation B1, bodhicitta B2, view B5, final effort B6.
Path of accumulation B2, joining B4, first ground B5, grounds 2–12.5 B6, thirteenth B7.
